stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: «The hall is justified by low cost, easy access and large capacity.» Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: En appliquant «Build a thesis / Name all three criteria. / Building a thesis with three criteria» au fragment, quelle option se justifie ?

options.text: The hall is cheap, so it is good enough.
The hall is justified by low cost, easy access and large capacity.
The hall looks nice, which is all that matters.
options.misconception: overstates the claim in the summary

options.text: The hall is new, so it must be better.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: a thesis with three criteria names all three. On that basis "The hall is justified by low cost, easy access and large capacity" is the supported choice. Option A ("The hall is cheap, so it is good enough") fails because it repeats thesis instead of extending; Option C ("The hall looks nice, which is all that matters") fails because it overstates the claim in the summary; Option D ("The hall is new, so it must be better") fails because it infers beyond the notice's scope.

questions.stem: La consigne de cet item est «Write a conclusion that adds / A good conclusion extends, not repeats. / A conclusion that adds rather than repeats». Quelle réponse en découle ?

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: the conclusion adds a payback point. questions.hint: A good conclusion extends, not repeats.
